claims.text: The proposed reference potential incorporates machine-learning-based approaches.
A machine-learning-based potential can capture complex atomic interactions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Capturing complex atomic interactions will improve representation of the configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
Improved representation of ab initio liquid configurations will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning-based reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states.
The proposed method applies at and near the alloys' high melting temperatures.
Applicability is expected within the high-entropy-alloy composition regime.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction depends on the specific implementation of the machine-learning approach.
Free-energy calculations comparing the new potential with ab initio results can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a significant reduction in path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
